summary.en: Connect actions through classes and lambdas while keeping calculation rules separate from Swing.
summary.bn: ক্লাস বা ল্যাম্বডা দিয়ে ক্লিকের কাজ লেখো আর হিসাবের নিয়ম জিইউআই থেকে আলাদা রাখো।

notes: All programs use Java 17 APIs and language rules.

sections.title: Connect a user action to one meaningful operation
Register a class or a lambda listener
Trace a click from the queue back to the label
Make background completion an explicit event
Avoid duplicate effects and hidden model dependencies
Use stable event APIs on Java 17
Keep event translation thin and model rules reusable

examples.title: A lambda-driven calculator
examples.explanationHtml: The lambda parses inputs and delegates addition to Calculator. Validation messages replace the result label.
examples.outputNote: Enter 7 and 12 in Add calculator, then click Add to see 19. Enter x to see Enter whole numbers; 1001 gives Use -1000..1000.

examples.title: The same calculation through a named listener
examples.explanationHtml: AddListener receives its dependencies explicitly and implements the same event contract as the lambda.
examples.outputNote: The named-listener calculator has the same controls and validation as the first version. Check negative values and invalid text.

examples.title: A counter with a separate model
examples.explanationHtml: Each action increments the Counter object. The label is a display of that state.
examples.outputNote: Click Increment twice to see 2 in Click counter. The model starts from zero each time the application launches.

practice.title: Calculator controller without a window
practice.statementHtml: Read two nonempty tokens. Parse int operands, each required to lie in -1000..1000. Print their sum, FORMAT for an unparsable token, or RANGE for parsed values outside the bounds. No prompt.
hints: Parse first, then call the bounded model.

practice.title: Drive the counter model
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..10000) simulated click actions. Call Counter.increment n times and print value. Create no Swing controls and print no prompt.
hints: The label should not store model state.

practice.title: Repair duplicate registration
practice.statementHtml: A refresh method attaches another Add listener every time it runs. After three refreshes one click adds three entries. Propose a repair.
practice.answerHtml: Register once during construction, or remove the previous listener before replacing it. Keep refresh focused on rendering current state rather than adding more action effects.
hints: Count registrations rather than mouse clicks.

practice.title: Separate a slow search
practice.statementHtml: A search listener reads fields, performs a slow search and updates labels. Identify which steps belong on which thread.
practice.answerHtml: Read field text on the EDT, pass ordinary values to a background task, and deliver the result update on the EDT. Manage overlapping requests so stale results cannot replace a newer search.
hints: Components stay on the EDT; expensive work does not.

quiz.prompt: What result should the calculator view display for -7 plus 12?
quiz.explanation: The model adds the two signed integers.

quiz.prompt: What counter value should two click actions display?
quiz.explanation: The plain model retains both increments without reading label text.

quiz.prompt: Does invalid field text reach the arithmetic call?
quiz.explanation: Parsing fails, so normal calculation is skipped and FORMAT is reported.

quiz.prompt: What connects a listener to a button?
Which dependency should an arithmetic model avoid?
quiz.explanation: The view owns labels while the model owns arithmetic.

quiz.prompt: What happens if the same handler is registered twice?
options: One action can invoke it twice
quiz.explanation: Manage registration explicitly to avoid duplicate effects.

quiz.prompt: Why prefer ActionListener over mouse-only handling for a button action?
options: Actions can also come from keyboard activation
quiz.explanation: The action abstraction represents activation beyond physical mouse input.

quiz.prompt: Where should a worker deliver a final Swing label update?
quiz.explanation: Component updates follow Swing thread ownership.

quiz.prompt: Which input failure should the calculator catch narrowly?
quiz.explanation: Precise conversion handling avoids hiding unrelated programming failures.

keyPoints.en: Register listeners on the component producing the action.
keyPoints.bn: যে কম্পোনেন্ট অ্যাকশন দেয়, তার সঙ্গে লিসেনার যোগ করো।

keyPoints.en: Named classes and lambdas implement the same action contract.
keyPoints.bn: নাম দেওয়া ক্লাস আর ল্যাম্বডা দুটো দিয়েই অ্যাকশন লিসেনার লেখা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Parse view text before calling a numeric model.
keyPoints.bn: জিইউআইর টেক্সট সংখ্যায় বদলে তারপর মডেলকে দাও।

keyPoints.en: Keep model rules independent of Swing components.
keyPoints.bn: মডেলের নিয়ম সুইং কম্পোনেন্ট থেকে আলাদা রাখো।
EDT-র লিসেনারের কাজ দ্রুত শেষ করো।

examQuestions.question: Trace a calculator click from text fields to a result label.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The EDT invokes the listener. The listener reads and parses text, calls a bounded model operation, then displays the result. Parsing failure updates a useful message without calling arithmetic.

examQuestions.question: Compare a named ActionListener with a lambda.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Both implement actionPerformed. A named class can expose dependencies and reusable state clearly. A lambda reduces syntax for a short local handler.

examQuestions.question: Explain model-view separation in a click counter.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Counter owns the integer and increment operation. The listener coordinates an action. The label renders Counter.value rather than storing and parsing the authoritative count.
